decisions.context: Each card transaction needs a synchronous fraud score before authorization. The brief does not specify an API protocol.
decisions.rationale: Tens-of-milliseconds scoring decides in favor of a direct request and response interface. This accepts a network hop; the design space does not establish that REST meets a specific latency target.
consequences: The authorization path depends on the prediction service.
Measure end-to-end latency under peak load.

decisions.context: Scoring runs in the authorization path, and the service must remain available during peaks. Capacity reduction to zero risks cold-start delay.

alternatives.label: Replicated mutable model instances
cons: Availability: shared mutable state complicates operation

decisions.rationale: Peak availability decides in favor of elastic capacity. This gives up some cost efficiency to avoid relying on scale-to-zero for an authorization-time request.
consequences: Set capacity and scaling limits against observed peak traffic.
Monitor latency and resource use as load changes.

decisions.context: The model must score live transactions as part of authorization. The system therefore needs a production runtime that can expose real-time predictions.

alternatives.label: Model-as-a-service deployment
pros: Peak availability: service can scale independently

alternatives.label: Monolithic application architecture
pros: Low latency: avoids a separate model service call
cons: Peak availability: model and application scale together

alternatives.label: Containerized offline prediction service
cons: Low latency: offline scoring misses live authorization

decisions.rationale: Peak availability decides in favor of an independently deployable prediction service that can scale with demand. It adds a service boundary, so latency must be measured across the full authorization path.
consequences: Deploy and operate the model service alongside the authorization system.
Keep the service call within the scoring latency budget.

decisions.context: Auditors must be able to determine which model version and features produced each score. This requires retaining identifiers and linking the score to its serving and feature context.

alternatives.label: Comprehensive ML lifecycle traceability
pros: Audit traceability: links lifecycle artifacts and datasets
cons: Audit traceability: more metadata to govern

alternatives.label: Artifact version control
cons: Audit traceability: limited context for features and runs

alternatives.label: Pipeline and experiment version control
pros: Audit traceability: connects pipelines and experiments
cons: Audit traceability: serving context may remain unlinked

decisions.rationale: Audit traceability decides in favor of linking model artifacts, datasets, runs, metadata, and deployment status. This requires governing more metadata than artifact versioning alone.
consequences: Record the model version and feature identifiers with each score.
Preserve links from serving records to model and data lineage.

decisions.context: The system must keep serving at peak and later explain which features were used. Monitoring inputs and feature behavior can reveal changes that threaten score quality or indicate a changed scoring context.

alternatives.label: Input and feature-drift monitoring
cons: Peak availability: monitoring adds operational work

alternatives.label: Service-health and data-quality monitoring
pros: Peak availability: tracks latency and uptime
cons: Audit traceability: does not by itself link each score to its features

alternatives.label: Passive production operation
cons: Peak availability: failures may go unseen

decisions.rationale: Audit traceability decides in favor of monitoring feature inputs and their changes. This requires operational effort; monitoring alone does not prove which exact feature values produced an individual score.
consequences: Track feature schemas and distributions in production.
Store per-score feature identifiers with the model version.

uncovered: Exact latency budget, percentile target, and timeout or fallback behavior.
Peak transaction volume, availability target, and regional failover requirements.
Per-score feature-value retention, explanation format, and audit retention period.
Model family, training and evaluation strategy, and promotion criteria.
